notes.tone: All four are HEROES in their own stories -> warm humor, from mannerism and earnestness, not cutting wit. Death is the only dry voice at this table.
notes.difficulty: Beginner table. Contempt is real but not cruel; these are dignified men, not bullies. The sting is being dismissed, not insulted.
notes.dealer_plant: The single 'the dealer arranged it' line for this table is wh_plant_01. Do NOT add a second.
notes.washington: Barely speaks until heads-up. His silence is the point — every line he gets lands harder because he spends most of the table saying nothing.
notes.leak_rule: No line may reference hand strength while cards are live.
notes.voice: Champion (Washington) + Death are voiced. Lincoln/Roosevelt/FDR are text + vocalization for now.

respect_tiers.0: Contempt. The player is not addressed by any name.
respect_tiers.1: Grudging notice. A dismissive nickname appears.
respect_tiers.2: Real address. They speak TO the player, not about them.
respect_tiers.3: Title. Earned. Washington uses it first.

table_intro.speaker: death
table_intro.text: Four men who each believed the republic would not outlast them. It did. They find that less comforting than you would think.

table_intro.speaker: death
table_intro.text: I have dealt to all of them before. Under different circumstances.
table_intro.foreshadow: Reads as poker flavor. Actually means he was present at each of their deaths. True, as always.

table_intro.speaker: death
table_intro.text: They have agreed to make room for you. Not gladly.

dealer_plant.speaker: roosevelt
dealer_plant.text: General — who let this one in?

dealer_plant.speaker: washington
dealer_plant.note: Washington's first words at the table. Weight comes from his silence.

dealer_plant.speaker: roosevelt
dealer_plant.note: THE SHRUG. Nobody questions the dealer. The player never gets an answer.

roosevelt_fdr.relationship: Fifth cousins. FDR married Theodore's niece Eleanor, and Theodore personally gave her away at the wedding. Real family friction — the richest pair at this table.

exchanges.speaker: roosevelt
exchanges.text: Franklin. Still playing every hand like it's a negotiation.

exchanges.speaker: fdr
exchanges.text: And you still play yours like a cavalry charge.

exchanges.speaker: roosevelt
exchanges.text: It worked.

exchanges.speaker: fdr
exchanges.text: Once.

exchanges.speaker: roosevelt
exchanges.text: You married my niece, Franklin. I have never forgiven the presumption.

exchanges.speaker: fdr
exchanges.text: You gave her away, Theodore. At the ceremony. Personally.

exchanges.speaker: roosevelt
exchanges.text: Under duress.

exchanges.speaker: fdr
exchanges.text: Cousin. You're bleeding chips.

exchanges.speaker: roosevelt
exchanges.text: I am investing them.

exchanges.speaker: roosevelt
exchanges.text: Franklin, you have smiled at everyone at this table tonight.

exchanges.speaker: fdr
exchanges.text: And every one of them smiled back. That is the job, Theodore.

exchanges.speaker: roosevelt
exchanges.text: The job is to win.

exchanges.speaker: fdr
exchanges.text: That is winning. It just doesn't make as much noise.

exchanges.speaker: fdr
exchanges.text: Uncle Ted —

exchanges.speaker: roosevelt
exchanges.text: Do not call me that at the table.

exchanges.speaker: fdr
exchanges.text: Eleanor does.

exchanges.speaker: roosevelt
exchanges.text: Eleanor has earned it.

needles.speaker: roosevelt
needles.text: Ha! Franklin folds! Somebody write it down; nobody will believe it.

needles.speaker: fdr
needles.text: Nobody ever believes anything about me, Theodore. It's very restful.

needles.speaker: fdr
needles.text: There goes the cavalry. Round the long way, for once.

needles.speaker: roosevelt
needles.text: A strategic withdrawal, cousin. I've read about them.

lincoln_roosevelt.relationship: Patience against force. Lincoln folds and waits; Theodore cannot sit still. The comic engine of the table.

exchanges.speaker: roosevelt
exchanges.text: You have folded six hands, Abraham.

exchanges.speaker: lincoln
exchanges.text: Seven.

exchanges.speaker: roosevelt
exchanges.text: That is not poker. That is a filibuster.

exchanges.speaker: lincoln
exchanges.text: It has worked so far.

exchanges.speaker: lincoln
exchanges.text: Theodore. You do not have to win every hand.

exchanges.speaker: roosevelt
exchanges.text: I do not have to. I choose to.

exchanges.speaker: lincoln
exchanges.text: That is the part that worries me.

exchanges.speaker: roosevelt
exchanges.text: Abraham, how do you stand it? Sitting there, hand after hand?

exchanges.speaker: lincoln
exchanges.text: I once waited two months for the right battle before I said anything important.

exchanges.speaker: roosevelt
exchanges.text: Two months! I'd have gone mad.

exchanges.speaker: lincoln
exchanges.text: You'd have gone to Cuba.

exchanges.speaker: lincoln
exchanges.text: They tell me you were shot once, and gave the speech anyway.

exchanges.speaker: roosevelt
exchanges.text: The bullet went through the manuscript first. Fifty pages, folded double. Long speeches save lives!

exchanges.speaker: lincoln
exchanges.text: Mine was two minutes.

exchanges.speaker: roosevelt
exchanges.text: ...Well. Yours was better.

needles.speaker: roosevelt
needles.text: Folded again, Abraham! That's not patience, that's hibernation.

needles.speaker: lincoln
needles.text: Bears come out in the spring, Theodore. Rested.

needles.speaker: lincoln
needles.text: Theodore. Did you just go around an obstacle?

washington_table.relationship: They all defer to him. He rarely responds. Comedy from the size of the gap.

exchanges.speaker: roosevelt
exchanges.text: General — tell him he plays too slowly.

exchanges.speaker: washington
exchanges.text: He plays correctly.

exchanges.speaker: roosevelt
exchanges.text: That is the same thing!

exchanges.speaker: fdr
exchanges.text: The General has not spoken in an hour.

exchanges.speaker: lincoln
exchanges.text: He has spoken twice. You were not listening.

exchanges.speaker: fdr
exchanges.text: General. About your two-term tradition.

exchanges.speaker: washington
exchanges.text: Yes.

exchanges.speaker: fdr
exchanges.text: I did give it a great deal of thought.

exchanges.speaker: washington
exchanges.text: Four times, I am told.

exchanges.speaker: lincoln
exchanges.text: I said once that nobody could add glory to the name of Washington.

exchanges.speaker: washington
exchanges.text: [inclines his head, very slightly]

exchanges.speaker: lincoln
exchanges.text: I stand by it. I'd just like to take a pot off him.

exchanges.speaker: roosevelt
exchanges.text: General! You crossed the Delaware at night, in the ice!

exchanges.speaker: washington
exchanges.text: I did.

exchanges.speaker: roosevelt
exchanges.text: Bully! What was it like?

exchanges.speaker: washington
exchanges.text: Cold.

needles.speaker: washington
needles.text: [looks at FDR for a long moment, and says nothing at all]

needles.speaker: fdr
needles.text: I know that look. My mother had that look.

needles.speaker: washington
needles.text: [inclines his head to Lincoln: one commander to another]

needles.speaker: lincoln
needles.text: Thank you, General. I'd rather have had the pot.

needles.speaker: roosevelt
needles.text: The General folded! To me! Did everyone see that?

lincoln_fdr.relationship: Two wartime presidents. Quiet mutual recognition — the table's one serious beat. Use sparingly.

exchanges.speaker: fdr
exchanges.text: You had a war as well.

exchanges.speaker: lincoln
exchanges.text: I had the one where we were the enemy.

exchanges.speaker: fdr
exchanges.text: ...Yes. I would take mine.

tier_0.speaker: roosevelt
tier_0.text: Sit down, tenderfoot. Try not to embarrass yourself.

tier_0.speaker: fdr
tier_0.text: Don't trouble yourself. Nobody remembers who came fourth.

tier_0.speaker: lincoln
tier_0.text: You have the look of a man who has read about poker.

tier_0.speaker: roosevelt
tier_0.text: We are not here to teach. Watch, or leave.

tier_1.speaker: fdr
tier_1.text: You are harder to read than you were an hour ago.

tier_1.speaker: lincoln
tier_1.text: You are learning. That is more than most manage here.

tier_1.speaker: washington
tier_1.text: [looks at the player for the first time]

tier_2.speaker: roosevelt
tier_2.text: {name}. There — the tenderfoot is retired. I was one myself, out in the Dakotas, until I wasn't.
tier_2.note: First use of the player's real name. Roosevelt coined 'tenderfoot', so he retires it. True: he ranched in Dakota Territory in the 1880s and arrived there as an Eastern greenhorn.

tier_2.speaker: roosevelt
tier_2.text: Very well. You have earned the chair. Now earn the pot.

tier_2.speaker: fdr
tier_2.text: I have stopped underestimating you. Take that as the compliment it is.

tier_2.speaker: lincoln
tier_2.text: I have watched a great many men bluff. You are getting good at it.

tier_3.speaker: washington
tier_3.note: First time anyone gives the player a title. Washington uses it first.

tier_3.speaker: roosevelt
tier_3.text: By God, I hope you take the whole tour.

tier_3.speaker: fdr
tier_3.text: When you reach the last table — and you will — remember they are only men. Mostly.
tier_3.foreshadow: 'Mostly.' Reads as a joke about monsters ahead. Isn't.

tier_3.speaker: lincoln
tier_3.text: Whatever waits at the end of your road, I suspect it has been waiting a long while.
tier_3.foreshadow: Sounds like a homily. Is a description of the dealer sitting three feet away.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Take your time. I have nothing but.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: The cards do not care who you were.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: They all played like this at the end.
death_asides.foreshadow: Reads as 'desperate players play alike.' Means what it says.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: All of it. Every man at this table has staked more than chips before.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Don't trouble yourself over him. He has had worse evenings.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Blinds up. In this house nothing is meant to last more than two terms. One of them disagreed.
death_asides.note: True: Washington set the two-term precedent; FDR broke it.

champion_headsup.speaker: washington
champion_headsup.text: I have had few opponents. Fewer I remembered.

champion_headsup.speaker: washington
champion_headsup.text: Discipline is not caution. You will learn the difference or you will not.

lincoln.speaker: lincoln
lincoln.text: I lost to Douglas once. It did not go the way he expected afterwards.
lincoln.note: True: lost the 1858 Senate race to Stephen Douglas, beat him for the presidency in 1860.

lincoln.speaker: lincoln
lincoln.text: Don't get up. I'll sit by the fire and see how it comes out.

roosevelt.speaker: roosevelt
roosevelt.text: Bully! Well fought. I was shot once and gave the speech anyway — I can stand this.

roosevelt.speaker: roosevelt
roosevelt.text: Out! Fine. I am going for a walk. Over the obstacles, not around them.
roosevelt.note: His 'point to point' walks, famous for going over, under or through obstacles, never around.

fdr.speaker: fdr
fdr.text: Splendid. I shall tell everyone I let you have that one, and half of them will believe me.

fdr.speaker: fdr
fdr.text: [laughs as though it had been his idea all along, and settles his cape]

washington.speaker: washington
washington.text: I know how to leave a room.
washington.note: He resigned his commission in 1783 and declined a third term in 1796.

washington.speaker: washington
washington.text: [rises, bows to the table, and goes]

player_busted.speaker: death
player_busted.text: It happens. Not usually this early. Shall I deal again?

player_busted.speaker: lincoln
player_busted.text: Don't take it hard. I was beaten plenty of times before anyone let me win.

player_busted.speaker: roosevelt
player_busted.text: Up, up! Everyone worth knowing has been knocked flat. Come back and have another go.

champion_defeat.speaker: washington
champion_defeat.text: The chair is yours. I never held one I did not intend to give up.

champion_defeat.speaker: death
champion_defeat.text: One. Seven remain. They will have heard by the time you arrive.
champion_defeat.foreshadow: Sets up per-table respect propagation AND implies Death travels ahead of you.
